classes.name: Elección de Presidente y Vicepresidente de la República
classes.note: Direct popular election since the constitutional reform of 1910 (Acto Legislativo 3 de 1910), first held in February 1914; electoral colleges chose the president under the 1886 Constitution until then (class presidente_1886). Plurality until 1990; since 1994 an absolute majority or a runoff three weeks later between the top two (Constitución art. 190), and the vice president is elected on the same ticket (art. 202). Four-year terms; immediate re-election was allowed only from 2006 to 2014. Colombians abroad vote. The Frente Nacional rotated the presidency between the two traditional parties from 1958 to 1974. Since 2018 the runner-up ticket takes seats in the Senate and the House (Ley 1909 de 2018 art. 24).
classes.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/constitucion_politica_1991.html (art. 190: "por la mitad más uno de los votos ... Si ningún candidato obtiene dicha mayoría, se celebrará una nueva votación que tendrá lugar tres semanas más tarde")
classes.finest_note: mesa (polling table) inside the puesto de votación; mesa-by-mesa files on the Observatorio for 2018, 2022, and 2026, and per-year statistics databases for 1998 to 2014

cadence.runoff_rule: If no ticket wins half the votes plus one, the top two meet three weeks later (Constitución art. 190)
cadence.administered_by: Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil; the Consejo Nacional Electoral declares the election
cadence.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/decreto_2241_1986_pr004.html (art. 207: corporaciones públicas el segundo domingo de marzo, Presidente el último domingo de mayo); http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/constitucion_politica_1991.html (art. 190)

classes.name: Elección presidencial por asambleas electorales (Constitución de 1886)
classes.note: Under the 1886 Constitution the president was chosen for six-year terms by electoral assemblies (asambleas electorales) that voters elected in each district, until Acto Legislativo 3 de 1910 restored direct election from 1914. Earlier presidents of the Granadine and federal republics (1821-1885) were chosen under other constitutions by electors, direct vote, or the votes of the states.
classes.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/constitucion_politica_1991.html (art. 190 replaces the regime of the 1886 Constitution; see the Antecedentes)
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of the electoral college returns is online: the Registraduría's published series start with the 1997-1998 statistics CDs, and the nineteenth-century returns sit in the Diario Oficial and congressional archives, which are not digitized as results.

classes.name: Elección de Senado de la República
classes.note: 100 senators in one national constituency and two more in a national special constituency for indigenous communities (Constitución art. 171); Colombians abroad vote. Lists with or without a preferential vote; seats by cifra repartidora (D'Hondt) among lists above 3% of valid votes (art. 263, since 2003; largest remainders before). Two contests per election: the national and the indigenous constituency. Seats that no ballot fills sit outside the contest: the runner-up presidential ticket (one seat since 2018, Ley 1909 de 2018 art. 24) and five seats guaranteed to the party of the former FARC-EP for 2018-2026 (Acto Legislativo 03 de 2017). Before 1991 senators were elected by department (class senado_1886).
classes.finest_note: mesa; mesa-by-mesa files for 2022 and 2026 on the Observatorio, statistics databases for 1998-2014

classes.name: Elección de Senado por departamentos (Constitución de 1886)
classes.note: Under the 1886 Constitution senators represented the departments: the departmental assemblies chose them until direct popular election by department replaced that in the 1940s, and lists were elected by electoral quotient in each department with the House until the 1991 Constitution created the national constituency. The Congress elected in 1990 was dissolved by the Constituent Assembly in 1991.
classes.disposition_reason: No official machine-readable results before 1997: the Registraduría's Observatorio begins with the 1997-1998 statistics CDs, the printed Estadísticas Electorales volumes are not online, and www.registraduria.gov.co refuses automated requests (HTTP 403).

classes.name: Elección de Cámara de Representantes, circunscripciones territoriales
classes.note: Each department and Bogotá, D.C. forms a constituency with two representatives plus one per 365,000 inhabitants over the first 365,000 (Constitución art. 176): 33 constituencies, with 161 territorial seats in 2022 and 2026, plus the raizal seat inside San Andrés. Lists by cifra repartidora above half the quotient (a third of it where two are elected; plurality where one is). Before 1991 the departments, intendencias, and comisarías elected the House with the Senate. The non-territorial seats are class camara_especial and the peace seats class camara_citrep.

classes.name: Elección de la Asamblea Nacional Constituyente
classes.note: Seventy members elected on 9 December 1990 in one national constituency by electoral quotient, after the vote of 27 May 1990 approved convening the assembly (class consulta_nacional); it wrote the 1991 Constitution and closed on 4 July 1991. Constitución art. 260 still lists the members of a Constituent Assembly among elected officers, and art. 376 lets Congress put a new assembly to the voters.
classes.disposition_reason: No official results file is online: the Registraduría's Observatorio starts with the 1997-1998 statistics CDs, and www.registraduria.gov.co, which hosts its historical publications, refuses automated requests (HTTP 403).

classes.name: Consultas populares e interpartidistas de partidos y movimientos políticos
classes.note: Open primaries that parties, movements, and coalitions convene to choose candidates, run by the Registraduría with ordinary-election rules and binding on the participants (Ley 1475 de 2011 arts. 5-7; Ley 130 de 1994 before). National presidential consultas are held with the March Congress election (the Liberal consulta of 1990 and 1994, party consultas in 2006, 2009, 2010, and 2014, and interparty consultas in 2018, 2022, and 2026); parties also hold separate-day and local consultas, as in October 2025. Party-internal votes the Registraduría does not run are class votos_no_estatales.

classes.name: Referendo, plebiscito y consulta popular nacional
classes.name_en: National referendums, plebiscites, and popular consultations
classes.note: The plebiscite of 1 December 1957 that founded the Frente Nacional; the official count of the consultation of 27 May 1990 on convening a constituent assembly; the constitutional referendum of 25 October 2003 (15 questions, Ley 796 de 2003, only one reached the turnout quorum); the plebiscite of 2 October 2016 on the peace agreement (Ley 1806 de 2016); and the anticorruption popular consultation of 26 August 2018 (seven questions, short of the quorum). Referendums, plebiscites, and consultations follow Ley 134 de 1994 and Ley 1757 de 2015 and Constitución arts. 103, 104, 170, 377, and 378.
classes.finest_note: mesa for 2016 and 2018 in the Registraduría's result sites; department and municipality in its bulletins

cadence.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/ley_1757_2015.html

classes.name: Elecciones que hace el Congreso (organismos de control, Consejo Nacional Electoral, magistrados)
classes.note: Congress in full session elects the nine members of the Consejo Nacional Electoral by cifra repartidora (Constitución art. 264) and the Comptroller General; the Senate elects the Constitutional Court's magistrates and the Procurator General from shortlists, and the House the Ombudsman. Until 1991 Congress also elected the presidential designado.
classes.disposition_reason: Votes of Congress on shortlisted officers, recorded in the Gaceta del Congreso; they are appointments by a legislature rather than elections, as the archive treats other countries' confirmations.

classes.name: Cargos judiciales y de control
classes.note: No judicial or law-enforcement office is filled by popular vote: the high courts co-opt their members or the Senate elects them, the Supreme Court elects the Attorney General (Fiscal General) from the President's shortlist, and municipal ombudsmen (personeros) and comptrollers are chosen by councils and assemblies.
classes.disposition_reason: No judicial, prosecutorial, or police office is elected by voters in Colombia.

classes.name: Elecciones no organizadas por la Organización Electoral
classes.name_en: Votes the electoral organization does not run (indigenous cabildos, community action boards, party-internal votes)
classes.note: Indigenous cabildos and resguardo authorities chosen by their own customs (Constitución art. 330), Afro-Colombian community councils, about 64,000 juntas de acción comunal, and party-internal votes without the Registraduría elect their officers under their own rules.
classes.disposition_reason: Not run, scrutinized, or published by the Registraduría or the Consejo Nacional Electoral; they are civil-society and customary elections.

classes.name: Elección de Gobernadores
classes.note: Popular election of the 32 governors by plurality since 27 October 1991 (the President appointed them before); three-year terms from 1992 and four-year terms from 2004, without immediate re-election (Constitución art. 303). The runner-up takes a seat in the assembly since 2019 (Ley 1909 de 2018 art. 25). Atypical elections fill vacancies more than 18 months before the term ends.
classes.finest_note: mesa, with the comuna of each polling place; mesa-by-mesa files for 2019 and 2023

classes.name: Elección de Consejos Intendenciales y Comisariales
classes.name_en: Councils of the intendencias and comisarías (national territories), before 1991
classes.note: The national territories (intendencias and comisarías) elected councils with the departmental assemblies until the 1991 Constitution made them departments (Código Electoral art. 209 still names the consejeros intendenciales y comisariales).
classes.disposition_reason: No official results published online for elections before 1997; the Registraduría's printed statistics are not digitized and www.registraduria.gov.co refuses automated requests (HTTP 403).

classes.name: Elección de Alcaldes
classes.note: Popular election of mayors since 13 March 1988 (Acto Legislativo 1 de 1986): two-year terms to 1992, three-year terms 1994-2000, and four-year terms since 2003, without immediate re-election (Constitución art. 314). Plurality, except Bogotá's Alcalde Mayor, who since 2023 needs 40% and a ten-point lead or faces a runoff three weeks later (art. 323). San Andrés island and the 18 non-municipalized areas elect no mayor. Atypical elections fill vacancies more than 18 months before the term ends.

classes.name: Elección de Concejos Municipales y Distritales
classes.name_en: Municipal and district councils (including Bogotá's Concejo Distrital)
classes.note: Each municipality elects a council of 7 to 21 members (Constitución art. 312) and Bogotá a council of 45 (art. 323) in one municipality-wide list contest by cifra repartidora; 12,072 councillors in 2023. Councils were elected with the Congress every two years until 1988, with the mayors in 1988-1992, and on the territorial election day since 1994. The mayoral runner-up takes a council seat since 2019.

classes.name: Elección de Juntas Administradoras Locales (ediles)
classes.name_en: Local administrative boards of comunas, corregimientos, and Bogotá's localidades
classes.note: Each comuna (urban) or corregimiento (rural) that a council creates, and each of Bogotá's 20 localidades, elects a junta administradora local of at least five ediles (seven or more in Bogotá) by list on the territorial election day (Constitución arts. 318 and 323): 668 boards in 72 municipalities in 2019 and 699 in 76 in 2023. Bogotá's localities first elected theirs in 1992.

classes.name: Elección de Consejos Municipales, Distritales y Locales de Juventud
classes.note: Voters aged 14 to 28 elect municipal and district youth councils and local youth councils in districts' localities, on a single day the Registraduría sets apart from other elections, every four years (Ley 1622 de 2013 as amended by Ley 1885 de 2018, arts. 43 and 52); closed lists from parties, youth organizations, and independent lists. Held on 5 December 2021 and 19 October 2025.
classes.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/ley_1885_2018.html (art. 43: "La Registraduría Nacional tendrá a su cargo la organización y dirección de las elecciones para conformar los Consejos Municipales y Locales de Juventud")

classes.name: Consultas populares, referendos y plebiscitos departamentales, distritales y municipales
classes.note: Governors and mayors may put a question of departmental, district, or municipal concern to the voters, and citizens may initiate local referendums (Constitución arts. 104-106; Ley 134 de 1994 and Ley 1757 de 2015), as in the mining consultations of 2013-2018. Dates are set case by case; the Registraduría publishes each result in a bulletin.

classes.name: Revocatoria del mandato de gobernadores y alcaldes
classes.name_en: Recall votes against governors and mayors
classes.note: Citizens may petition to recall a governor or mayor after the first year of the term; the vote succeeds with more than half of the votes cast and turnout of at least 40% of the votes that elected the officer (Constitución art. 103; Ley 134 de 1994 and Ley 1757 de 2015 arts. 6 and 41). Most petitions fail before a vote, and no vote has yet reached the quorum.

cadence.locator: http://www.secretariasenado.gov.co/senado/basedoc/ley_1757_2015.html (art. 41)
